synthesis:draft.headline: SA1 experienced a 5-minute RRP spike to $4,981.0 at 02:05 ACST (16:35 UTC); the half-hour sample covering the peak was $899.44 and dispatch TOTALDEMAND at the 5-minute peak was 1,472.82 MW.
summary: Half-hour RRP sample covering the peak (interval end 2026-07-30T17:00:00Z) = 899.44 [ev0448].
DISPATCH_TOTALDEMAND during the 5-minute peak = 1,472.82 MW (DISPATCH_TOTALDEMAND, dispatch measure) [ev0434].
DISPATCH_NETINTERCHANGE during the 5-minute peak = -82.59 (net flow into SA1) [ev0435].
Across the window the unweighted mean 5-minute RRP = 416.71 $/MWh and the minimum 5-minute RRP = 75.14288 $/MWh [ev0883, ev0700].
Analysis threshold used = 300.0 $/MWh and 214 five-minute intervals met or exceeded that threshold in the window [ev1019, ev1018].
Actual operational demand in the half-hour containing the price extreme (interval end 2026-07-30T17:00:00Z) = 1,466.0 MW; the window maximum operational demand = 2,173.0 MW [ev0910, ev0895].
SCADA observations show notable unit output changes in the hours around the spike (examples: SNAPPER +99.46 MW, PPCCGT -76.51 MW, QPS5 -72.87 MW) [ev0937, ev0940, ev0949].
AEMO published a market notice reporting a 'Non-credible contingency event - SA region - 30/07/2026' (see published_findings) [c1].

numeric_claims.text: Half-hour RRP sample covering the peak
Number of 5-minute intervals at or above the analysis threshold
Operational demand in the half-hour containing the price extreme (interval end 2026-07-30T17:00:00Z)
SNAPPER observed change in the generation-change window
PPCCGT observed change in the generation-change window
QPS5 observed change in the generation-change window

possible_explanations.statement: A reduction in available generation capacity (observed as large SCADA output changes for some units) may have tightened supply and corresponded with the price spike.
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Compare unit outage and availability records, unit trip reports and rebid logs for the DUIDs with large SCADA changes (e.g. those with ev0937, ev0940, ev0949) to see if outages or availability reductions align with the 16:35 UTC spike.

possible_explanations.statement: Rapid SCADA changes in unit outputs may reflect trips or last‑minute dispatch/rebid activity that could coincide with the price spike.
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Inspect rebid archive, unit trip alarms and detailed SCADA logs for timestamps around 16:35 UTC to determine whether the observed SCADA changes were trips, manual dispatch changes or other events.

possible_explanations.statement: Interconnector flow conditions (the net interconnector flow into SA1 at the 5-minute peak was -82.59 MW) might have limited import capability around the interval and could be relevant to market tightness.
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Retrieve full interconnector flow time series and any constraint/change notices for Heywood/Murraylink (and other interconnectors) for the event window to check for limits or rapid flow changes coincident with the peak.

possible_explanations.statement: Recent AEMO reserve/LOR notices around 29 July 2026 may have affected participant bidding behaviour and might be relevant background to the event [c2][c3].
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Review the rebid archive and participant bidding around the event and compare with the market notices (see citations c2 and c3) to detect systematic bidding changes following those notices.

uncertainties: No retrieved document explicitly attributes the 16:35 UTC price spike to a specific cause within the exact interval.
Generation-change outputs are SCADA snapshots and do not by themselves identify whether a change was a trip, planned ramp or a rebid/dispatch action.
missing_evidence: Rebid archive and bid stack for SA1 for dispatch intervals 16:20–16:40 UTC (to identify marginal unit(s) and bid prices).
Unit outage and trip reports for generators with large SCADA changes (matching DUIDs in ev0937, ev0940, ev0949, ev0952).
Detailed interconnector flow time series and any constraint/limit notices for Heywood/Murraylink around the event window.
AEMO dispatch constraint and market intervention logs that might explain binding constraints or interventions at the interval.
